items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: A boy named Walter Baker and myself applied for the job of making fires in the stoves in the school... Walter Baker made the fires on one side, and I made the fires on the other.

ctx.x: I went to high school there for that semester, and then I came on back over to my home town and went back to my regular school. And shortly after that things got so rough in my home town until they started charging tuition to go to high school. I just forget how much the tuition was. I think it was $1.50 or $2.00 a month, or something like that.

A boy named Walter Baker and myself applied for the job of making fires in the stoves in the school in order to keep from paying the tuition. This was the only way I could go to school, because my father wasn't able to support me.

So, we got the job. This school building had eight rooms; four down and four up. Walter Baker made the fires on one side, and I made the fires on the other. And we did that for about a semester, a semester and a half. Things were getting rough. I got me a job shining shoes. I worked at that for a while, and got me a job -- water boy on the boiler job. I worked at that
